title: Hubflow: hierarchical workspace switcher + contextual rail for compact consoles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Redesign the left rail and workspace switcher to improve discoverability of per-workspace dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views while preserving compactness for high-density power users. Goals: (1) Provide a single, predictable entry point for workspace-level routes (dashboards, rollouts, billing, models) that minimizes cognitive overhead when switching context; (2) Surface per-route lightweight status (SLOs, active rollouts) without requiring full-page navigation; (3) Make the rail adaptable across viewport densities (compact, standard, expanded) and responsive to user roles. Constraints: must re-use existing console auth/route primitives, maintain accessibility (keyboard + screen reader), and fit within current left-rail CSS grid without heavy runtime changes to layout engine. Deliverables: Figma prototype (compact / expanded), micro-interaction spec (hover, focus, keyboard), developer handoff token set, annotated IA diagram, and usability test summary. Acceptance criteria: (A) PM/Eng signoff on navigation mapping and route fallthrough behavior; (B) Prototype tested with 6 power-user sessions showing >= 80% task success for workspace switch + find cost breakdown; (C) No regression on primary keyboard navigation patterns. Trade-offs considered: persist workspace quick-list in rail vs ephemeral command-palette experience (we chose persistent quick-list for discoverability and lower cognitive load for non-power users); exposing live SLO badges on every item vs only on pinned routes (we landed on route-level micro-badges to reduce noise). Related engineering constraints: route prefetching should avoid heavy KV cache warmups; suggested approach: prefetch metadata endpoints (workspace meta, route-summaries) not full dashboard payloads.
comments: 2026-02-27 - Aisha Patel: Initial concept uploaded to Figma. Two variants: Compact with condensed icons + inline micro-badges, and Flow where the workspace pill expands into a micro-menu. Included sample states for rollout in-progress and cost-anomaly alert.

2026-03-01 - Benji Morales (Eng): Reviewed IA mapping. Concern: inline micro-badges may add DOM nodes; asked for a version that uses CSS pseudo-elements or server-inserted SVG sprites to avoid reflow. Action: design to provide sprite-compatible assets and a no-badge fallback.
2026-03-03 - Maya Torres (PM): Asked to prioritize keyboard focus ring clarity and a11y labels for workspace avatars. Also requested telemetry events list for workspace-switch and badge clicks.

2026-03-05 - Claire Zhang: Iteration 2 uploaded — reduced icon count, introduced a persistent workspace quick-list (top of rail) and an affordance for 'More routes' that opens a contextual rail extension. Updated spec with ARIA attributes and keyboard flow (tab/shift-tab to nav, space/enter to open, arrow keys to move within expanded menu).

2026-03-07 - UX Research: Moderated 6 remote sessions with platform engineers. Findings: users appreciated persistent quick-list and micro-badges; confusion occurred when 'More routes' used ellipses icon (misinterpreted as settings). Recommendation: change label to 'Explore' with chevron affordance and add tooltip on hover.

2026-03-09 - Engineering Sync (Benji Morales): Agree on API contract for route-summaries: GET /v1/workspaces/:id/route_summaries returning small payload (route_id, title, status_badge, unread_counts). Engineering to implement server-side limiting and caching; UI to render skeletons while fetching.

2026-03-10 - Design Review: PM + Eng signoff on IA decisions; minor action items: provide high-contrast badge variants and a11y test checklist. Next: prepare developer handoff (tokens + annotated frames) and create GH PR referencing frontend-ux/hubflow branch.
Follow-ups: add performance budget notes to handoff, schedule cross-team rollout review with Support for announcing changes to orgs.
